topics.name: Send API and Orchestrator-Worker
topics.description: Dynamic fan-out with Send for map-reduce and orchestrator-worker workflows.
notes: ## Send API 与动态 fan-out
- 当并行分支的数量在编译时未知（如 map-reduce）时，用 Send 动态创建任务。
- Send(node, state) 接收两个参数：目标节点名，以及传给该节点的状态。
- Send 对象从条件边的路由函数中返回，每个 Send 对应一次下游节点调用，且各自拥有独立的输入 state。
```python
def continue_to_jokes(state: OverallState):
return [Send("generate_joke", {"subject": s}) for s in state["subjects"]]
builder.add_conditional_edges("generate_topics", continue_to_jokes, ["generate_joke"])
## Orchestrator-worker
- Orchestrator 拆分任务、把子任务分派给 worker、最后由 synthesizer 汇总结果。
- 子任务无法预先定义时使用此模式；worker 的数量与输入在运行时才确定。
- 每个 worker 有自己的 state（如 WorkerState），所有 worker 的输出写入同一个共享 key。
- 共享 key 需要 reducer，否则后写入的值会覆盖前面的值。
```python
completed_sections: Annotated[list, operator.add]  # 所有 worker 并行写入
- map 阶段之后用普通 add_edge 连接到汇总节点（reduce）。

topics.name: Supersteps, Parallelism and Deferred Nodes
topics.description: How parallel branches execute in supersteps and how to wait for multiple branches.
notes: ## Super-step 与并行执行
- LangGraph 基于 message passing，按离散的 super-step 执行（受 Pregel 启发）。
- super-step 是对图中节点的一次迭代：并行节点在同一个 super-step，串行节点分属不同 super-step。
- 一个节点有多条出边时，所有目标节点在下一个 super-step 并行执行。
- 每个 super-step 是事务性的：任一并行分支抛异常，本 step 的更新都不会应用到 state。
- 并行分支更新同一个 key 时用 reducer（如 operator.add）累积；并行更新的顺序不保证一致。
- 可用 RetryPolicy 重试失败节点，只会重试失败的分支。
## Defer 与等待多个分支
- 分支长度不同时，普通边会让汇合节点执行多次。
- add_node 时设置 defer=True：该节点会等到图中没有待处理任务后才执行。
```python
builder.add_node("d", d, defer=True)
builder.add_edge("b_2", "d")
builder.add_edge("c", "d")
- 列表形式的边 add_edge(["b_2", "c"], "d")：所有列出的节点完成后 d 只运行一次。
- 若列表中某个分支没有被选中，d 不会运行，也不会报错。
- 即使 d 设置了 defer=True，发给它的 Send 仍会单独调用它。

topics.name: Loops and Recursion Limit
notes: ## 循环与终止条件
- 带循环的图必须有终止机制：通常是一条条件边，在满足终止条件时路由到 END。
```python
def route(state: State) -> Literal["b", END]:
return END if len(state["aggregate"]) >= 7 else "b"
## Recursion limit
- recursion limit 限制单次执行最多的 super-step 数，超过后抛出 GraphRecursionError（来自 langgraph.errors）。
- 通过 config 设置；recursion_limit 是独立的顶层 key，不能放进 configurable。
```python
graph.invoke(inputs, config={"recursion_limit": 5})
- 带分支的循环按 super-step 计数：A、B、（C 与 D 并行）、A，一圈共四步。
## 主动处理：RemainingSteps
- 在 state 中声明 remaining_steps: RemainingSteps（managed value），表示距离上限还剩多少步。
- 路由函数据此提前走向 END 或 fallback 节点，图可以正常结束，不抛异常。
- 被动方式：在 invoke 之外 try/except GraphRecursionError，实现简单，但图已被终止。
- 当前步数也可从 config["metadata"]["langgraph_step"] 读取。

topics.name: Subgraphs and Streaming Modes
topics.description: Using subgraphs as nodes, Command.PARENT, and the main stream modes.
notes: ## Subgraph 作为节点
- subgraph 是被用作另一个图中节点的图。
- 共享 state key：直接 add_node("node_1", subgraph)，无需包装函数。
- 不同 schema（无共享 key）：在节点函数里转换 state、调用 subgraph.invoke，再把结果转换回父 state。
```python
def call_subgraph(state: State):
out = subgraph.invoke({"bar": state["foo"]})
return {"foo": out["bar"]}
- 从子图节点跳到父图节点：Command(update=..., goto=..., graph=Command.PARENT)。
- 更新父子共享的 key 时，父图 state 中该 key 必须定义 reducer。
## Streaming modes
- values：每步之后的完整 state；updates：每步各节点返回的增量更新（含节点名）。
- messages：来自 LLM 调用的 (message_chunk, metadata) 二元组，可按 metadata["langgraph_node"] 过滤。
- custom：节点内用 get_stream_writer() 发送自定义数据，需设置 stream_mode="custom"。
- 其他模式：checkpoints、tasks、debug（前两者需要 checkpointer）。
- 父图要看到子图的输出（包括 messages token）需设置 subgraphs=True。
- 可传入列表同时使用多个 stream_mode。

questions.title: What are the two arguments of Send?

options.text: The state to pass and the reducer to apply
The name of the node and the state to pass to it
The source node and the destination node
The node function and a retry policy

questions.explanation: Send takes the name of the target node first and the state to pass to that node second. It is not a source/destination pair like an edge.

questions.title: Fill in the class that dispatches one worker invocation per section.

options.text: Command
Branch
Send
Route

questions.explanation: The docs' orchestrator-worker example returns a list of Send objects from the conditional edge function. Command updates state and routes from a node, it is not used for this fan-out.

questions.title: How is generate_joke invoked after generate_topics finishes?

options.text: Once, receiving the whole OverallState
It fails because the number of edges must be known when the graph is compiled
Once, with only the last subject
Three times, each with its own input state such as {"subject": "lions"}

questions.explanation: Each Send creates a separate invocation of the target node with the state given in that Send. This is exactly why Send suits cases where the number of edges is unknown ahead of time.

questions.title: Which statements explain why Send is used for map-reduce? Select all that apply.

options.text: The number of items to process may be unknown until runtime
Each downstream invocation can receive a different input state
Every worker needs its own add_edge from the orchestrator declared at build time
Send objects are returned from a conditional edge function

questions.explanation: Send exists for cases where the edges are not known ahead of time and each downstream node needs its own state; it is returned from conditional edges. Declaring one static edge per worker is exactly what Send avoids.

questions.title: In the orchestrator-worker example, completed_sections is declared as Annotated[list, operator.add]. What is the purpose of the reducer?

options.text: It makes Send run the workers one after another
It accumulates the outputs that all workers write to the same key instead of overwriting them
It is required for Send to be accepted by add_conditional_edges
It limits how many workers can run

questions.explanation: All workers write to this key in parallel, and without a reducer each update would override the previous value. The reducer combines the worker outputs into one list for the synthesizer.

questions.title: Which workflow pattern fits tasks whose subtasks cannot be predefined, and uses Send to create workers dynamically?

options.text: Prompt chaining
Parallelization
Orchestrator-worker
Evaluator-optimizer

questions.explanation: In orchestrator-worker the orchestrator breaks the task into subtasks, delegates them to workers and synthesizes the results. Parallelization is for subtasks that can be predefined.

questions.title: In LangGraph's execution model, what is a super-step?

options.text: A single iteration over the graph nodes; nodes running in parallel belong to the same one
A single call to the LLM inside a node
A checkpoint saved after the graph ends
A group of nodes that share the same state schema

questions.explanation: Parallel nodes are part of the same super-step while sequential nodes belong to separate super-steps. The recursion limit also counts super-steps.

questions.title: Two nodes run in parallel in one superstep and one of them raises an exception. What happens to the state updates of that superstep?

options.text: The successful branch's update is applied and only the failed branch is skipped
None of the updates from that superstep are applied, because the superstep is transactional
All updates are applied but flagged as stale
The failed node is silently retried forever

questions.explanation: A superstep is transactional: if any parallel branch raises, the whole superstep errors and none of its updates reach the state. Retries only happen if you configure a RetryPolicy.

questions.title: When does node d run in this graph?
questions.codeSnippet:
builder.add_node("d", d, defer=True)
builder.add_edge(START, "a")
builder.add_edge("a", "b")
builder.add_edge("a", "c")
builder.add_edge("b", "b_2")
builder.add_edge("b_2", "d")
builder.add_edge("c", "d")
builder.add_edge("d", END)

options.text: In the same superstep as b and c
Twice: once after c and once after b_2
Once, only after b, b_2 and c have all finished
Never, because defer=True is only valid on the last node

questions.explanation: defer=True postpones d until there are no pending tasks, so it waits for the longer b branch to finish. Without defer, the branches of different lengths would trigger d more than once.

questions.title: Node d aggregates results but runs more than once because the branches have different lengths. What is the fix?
questions.codeSnippet:
builder.add_node("d", d)
builder.add_edge(START, "a")
builder.add_edge("a", "b")
builder.add_edge("a", "c")
builder.add_edge("b", "b_2")
builder.add_edge("b_2", "d")
builder.add_edge("c", "d")
builder.add_edge("d", END)

options.text: Set recursion_limit to 3
Add defer=True when adding node d
Replace add_edge("c", "d") with a Send to d
Move node d before node a

questions.explanation: With separate edges, d runs once per superstep in which an incoming branch completes, so uneven branches make it run repeatedly. Marking d with defer=True makes it wait until every selected branch has finished.

questions.title: You use builder.add_edge(["b_2", "c"], "d"), but a conditional edge earlier in the graph never selects the branch containing c. What happens?

options.text: d runs after b_2 alone
d never runs, and no error is raised
GraphRecursionError is raised
compile() raises an error

questions.explanation: A list of start nodes makes d wait for all of them; if one never runs, d never runs and nothing is reported. Updates from the branches that did complete stay in state but d does not consume them.

questions.title: Which statements about parallel branches in a superstep are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Updates from a parallel superstep may not be ordered consistently
A reducer such as operator.add accumulates values from parallel nodes instead of overwriting them
With a RetryPolicy, only the failing branches are retried
Parallel updates are always applied in alphabetical order of node names

questions.explanation: The docs warn that update order is not guaranteed, so write outputs to a separate field with an ordering value if you need a fixed order. There is no alphabetical ordering guarantee.

questions.title: Node d is added with defer=True, and a Send addressed to d is also issued. What happens to the Send?

options.text: It is ignored because d is deferred
It is merged into the single deferred run of d
It raises InvalidUpdateError
It still invokes d separately

questions.explanation: defer=True postpones the node until no tasks are pending anywhere in the graph, but a Send addressed to the node still invokes it separately. It does not get folded into the deferred run.

questions.title: What is the most common way to terminate a loop in a LangGraph graph?

options.text: Add a conditional edge that routes to END once a termination condition is met
Call graph.stop() inside a node
Return None from any node
Loops are not allowed in a StateGraph

questions.explanation: The docs add a conditional edge that routes to END when a termination condition is reached. Loops are allowed and are how agents alternate between model and tool nodes.

questions.title: Which error does LangGraph raise when a run exceeds its recursion limit?

options.text: RecursionError
TimeoutError
InvalidUpdateError
GraphRecursionError

questions.explanation: Once the configured number of super-steps is exceeded, LangGraph raises GraphRecursionError, importable from langgraph.errors. It is distinct from Python's built-in RecursionError.

questions.title: Fill in the managed-value type that tracks how many steps remain before the recursion limit.

options.text: StepCounter
RecursionLeft
ManagedStep
RemainingSteps

questions.explanation: RemainingSteps is a managed value that LangGraph populates for the duration of the run. Routing on it lets the graph end gracefully instead of raising GraphRecursionError.

questions.title: The developer wants to cap the run at 4 supersteps. What is wrong with how the limit is passed?

options.text: recursion_limit must be a standalone top-level config key, not nested inside configurable
recursion_limit must be passed as context= instead of config
GraphRecursionError cannot be caught with try/except
The limit must be set in builder.compile() only

questions.explanation: The docs state that recursion_limit is a standalone config key and should not be placed inside configurable like other user-defined configuration. The correct call is graph.invoke(inputs, {"recursion_limit": 4}).

questions.title: What happens when this graph is invoked?
questions.codeSnippet:
# every node appends its own letter to aggregate
def route(state: State) -> Literal["b", END]:
    return "b" if len(state["aggregate"]) < 7 else END

builder.add_edge(START, "a")
builder.add_conditional_edges("a", route)
builder.add_edge("b", "c")
builder.add_edge("b", "d")
builder.add_edge(["c", "d"], "a")
graph = builder.compile()
graph.invoke({"aggregate": []}, {"recursion_limit": 4})

options.text: It returns normally after one lap through a, b, c and d
It ends silently and returns the partial aggregate
It raises GraphRecursionError, because one lap takes four supersteps and the termination condition is not yet met
It finishes after three laps because c and d run in separate supersteps

questions.explanation: A lap is a (superstep 1), b (2), c and d in parallel (3), then a again (4), and the aggregate is still shorter than 7 after one lap. The limit of 4 is therefore exceeded and GraphRecursionError is raised.

questions.title: Which are advantages of the proactive RemainingSteps approach over catching GraphRecursionError? Select all that apply.

options.text: Graceful degradation inside the graph
The graph completes normally without raising an exception
No need to modify the graph logic
Intermediate state can be saved in checkpoints
Errors are handled centrally outside the graph in a try/except

questions.explanation: Proactive handling routes inside the graph before the limit is hit, so partial results can be returned and checkpointed. Not modifying graph logic and centralized try/except are advantages of the reactive approach.

questions.title: Which statements about using subgraphs are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: A subgraph is a graph used as a node in another graph
If parent and subgraph share state keys, a compiled subgraph can be passed directly to add_node
A subgraph must always be compiled with checkpointer=True
With different state schemas, you call the subgraph inside a node function and transform the state

questions.explanation: Shared keys allow adding the compiled subgraph directly, while different schemas need a wrapper node that maps state in and out. The default checkpointer setting is None (per-invocation), not True.

questions.title: The parent and the subgraph share no state keys. What should change?
questions.codeSnippet:
class SubgraphState(TypedDict):
    bar: str

class State(TypedDict):
    foo: str

# subgraph is a compiled StateGraph(SubgraphState)
builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("node_1", subgraph)
builder.add_edge(START, "node_1")

options.text: Add a reducer to foo
Compile the subgraph with checkpointer=False
Wrap the call in a node function that maps foo to bar, invokes the subgraph and maps the result back
Rename START to bar

questions.explanation: Passing a compiled subgraph directly only works when it shares keys with the parent. With different schemas, a wrapper node transforms the parent state into the subgraph input and the output back.

questions.title: The subgraph updates a key shared with the parent while navigating to a parent node. What must the parent state define?

options.text: A checkpointer on the subgraph
A context_schema for foo
A reducer for foo, e.g. Annotated[str, operator.add]
A static add_edge from node_a to node_b

questions.explanation: When a subgraph node sends updates to the parent for a key shared by both schemas via Command.PARENT, the parent must define a reducer for that key. A static edge would be redundant with goto and would run in addition to it.

questions.title: Which of these are valid stream_mode values? Select all that apply.

options.text: values
updates
trace
custom
nodes

questions.explanation: values streams the full state after each step, updates streams the per-node state updates, and custom streams data emitted with a stream writer. There are no stream modes named trace or nodes.

questions.title: What does stream_mode="messages" yield?

options.text: The full state after each step
2-tuples of (LLM token or message chunk, metadata) from LLM calls
Only the final AIMessage when the graph ends
Checkpoint events in the format of get_state()

questions.explanation: messages mode streams LLM output token by token as (message_chunk, metadata) pairs, and the metadata lets you filter by node or tags. The full state belongs to values mode and checkpoint events to checkpoints mode.

questions.title: Fill in the function that returns a writer for emitting custom stream data from a node.

options.text: get_writer
get_stream_writer
stream_writer
get_custom_stream

questions.explanation: get_stream_writer from langgraph.config returns the writer used to emit custom data, which is received when stream_mode includes "custom". The other names do not exist in langgraph.config.

questions.title: An agent built with create_agent is added as a node of a parent graph. Streaming the parent with stream_mode="messages" shows no tokens from the inner agent's LLM calls. What fixes it?

options.text: Pass subgraphs=True to the parent graph's stream call
Compile the inner agent with checkpointer=False
Switch to stream_mode="values"
Add defer=True to the agent node

questions.explanation: A compiled agent used as a node is a subgraph, and without subgraphs=True the parent stream does not emit its inner token chunks. Streaming the agent directly would work, which is why the problem only appears after wrapping.

questions.title: How do you make a graph start at different nodes depending on custom logic?

options.text: Call add_conditional_edges from the START node
Call add_edge(END, "node") with a lambda
Add several add_edge(START, ...) calls and compile with entry=None
Return a Send from the compile() call

questions.explanation: A conditional entry point is created with add_conditional_edges(START, routing_function), optionally with a mapping of outputs to node names. Plain add_edge from START is a fixed entry point.

questions.title: Which nodes run after node_a finishes?

options.text: Only my_other_node, because goto overrides static edges
Only node_b, because static edges take priority
Neither, because mixing them raises an error at compile time
Both node_b and my_other_node

questions.explanation: Command only adds dynamic edges, so static edges defined with add_edge still execute. For each node, use either Command or static edges to route, not both.
